title: Revealing the Biases of Large Language Models By Inferring Prior Distributions
abstract: arXiv:2611.18996v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been known to exhibit a wide range of social biases including name-nationality associations, occupation-gender associations and racial stereotypes. Existing approaches to evaluating these biases typically involve measuring surface-level behavior where a model is fed a dataset of prompts and its outputs are scored relative to ground-truth answers. Inspired by prior elicitation in cognitive science, we propose a different perspective that reconstructs latent bias as a prior underlying the model's behavior. We formulate the problem as a Bayesian inverse problem where, given prompt-response observations on a bias benchmark dataset, we infer a low-dimensional latent distribution that summarizes the model's stereotyping tendencies. translated_title: 通过推断先验分布揭示大语言模型的偏见
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLMs）已被证实存在广泛的社会偏见，包括姓名-国籍关联、职业-性别关联以及种族刻板印象。现有的偏见评估方法通常仅测量表面层面的行为：给模型输入一个提示数据集，然后根据真实答案对其输出进行评分。受认知科学中先验引出方法的启发，我们提出了一个不同的视角：将潜在偏见重构为模型行为背后的先验分布。我们将该问题表述为一个贝叶斯逆问题：在偏见基准数据集上，根据给定的提示-响应观测数据，推断出一个低维潜在分布来概括模型的刻板印象倾向。本文发展了相应的数学基础和一种实用的重建算法，并使用问答偏见基准数据集（BBQ）进行实验来推断先验分布。
tldr: 本文提出一种基于贝叶斯逆问题的新方法，通过从模型在偏见基准数据集上的提示-响应观测中推断低维潜在先验分布，来揭示和量化大语言模型深层的社会刻板印象倾向。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a novel Bayesian inverse problem approach that infers a low-dimensional latent prior distribution from prompt-response observations on bias benchmarks, revealing the deep-seated social stereotyping tendencies of large language models.
